description: The e-Prokurimi document-management path https://e-prokurimi.rks-gov.net/SPIN_PROD/APPLICATION/IPN/DocumentManagement/DokumentiFrm.aspx returned an Albanian login form (Emri i shfrytëzuesit / Fjalëkalimi), not a public notice list.

result.result_summary: Login wall on the notice-list form path. This is a HYPOTHESIS about that specific path only — individual notice detail pages under the same tree (DokumentPodaciFrm.aspx?id=) are search-engine indexed and appear publicly readable, and the platform documentation refers to a public 'Lista e Njoftimeve' view whose exact public URL I did not confirm.

why_it_matters: The collector must not assume a scrapeable HTML notice list on the portal. The OCDS API (ocdskrpp.rks-gov.net/krppAPI) should be the primary channel, with portal document fetches keyed by id resolved from the API.

description: No Serbian-language Kosovo-institution procurement search interface was located; sr-language queries returned Kosovo secondary legislation in Serbian on e-prokurimi.rks-gov.net plus Republic-of-Serbia sources (kim.gov.rs, paragraf.rs) that are jurisdictionally different.

result.result_summary: Serbian terminology for Kosovo notices is confirmed and usable ('javne nabavke', 'obaveštenje o dodeli ugovora', 'ugovor o uslugama'), and the platform does publish sr-language legislation, but I found no separate sr-language notice portal — the sr content lives inside the same platform.

why_it_matters: Serbian-language collection should be implemented as a language parameter/keyword set against the same national platform, not as a separate source. Serbia-hosted 'Kosovo' procurement pages must be excluded to avoid jurisdictional contamination.

description: No specific Kosovo public-sector award notice for ATM, POS, card-issuance or core-banking lots was surfaced by open web search in either sq or en within this scouting pass.

result.result_summary: Topical searches returned only foreign tenders (Ethiopia) and commercial aggregator landing pages. The only concrete Kosovo banking-adjacent notice found was a BQK life-insurance service award, which is not in scope.

why_it_matters: Absence of search-engine visibility is not absence of notices — these lots are almost certainly present inside the platform but invisible to general web search because notice bodies are behind the application. Confirms that keyword search must be run against the OCDS API fields (tendername, Award), not against Google.

description: The KRPP OCDS API endpoints were read from the auto-generated ASP.NET Help page, which states 'No documentation available' for every method; response formats, DataFormat values, pagination behaviour, rate limits and whether CPV codes are exposed are all undocumented.

result.result_summary: Endpoint list is reliable; endpoint semantics are not. No authentication is mentioned, which suggests open access but does not prove it.

why_it_matters: An implementation pass must empirically probe Award and TenderRelease before the collector design is fixed; in particular whether banking/payments lots can be filtered by CPV or only by free-text tendername determines the whole keyword strategy.

description: The OCP Data Registry entry for Kosovo PPRC explicitly documents quality problems in the published OCDS: null values and field-name typos across a corpus of 75,710 tenders / 211,313 parties.

result.result_summary: Known-defective official open data, still the best available machine channel.

why_it_matters: Any supplier-concentration or value analysis built on this feed needs defensive parsing and a field-name normalisation layer, or banking/payments lots will be silently dropped.

description: No published BQK tender or award notice specifically for the ATS/RTGS/ACH interbank payment system was located, in sq, sr or en, despite targeted searches. Only descriptive pages about the system's 2016 go-live were found.

result.result_summary: Four query formulations across three languages returned payment-system descriptions, SWIFT directories and commercial aggregators, but zero procurement documents naming RTGS/ACH.

why_it_matters: The cell rationale assumes BQK tenders payment infrastructure visibly. If those procurements are conducted under BQK's own rulebook, restricted procedures, or vendor-direct renewal, the tender record will never surface them and the pipeline must rely on financial statements, audit reports and vendor-side announcements instead.

description: Every automated fetch of bqk-kos.org returned HTTP 403 Forbidden — the tenders listing page and two PDFs (procurement rulebook, financial statements).

result.result_summary: 3/3 fetch attempts on bqk-kos.org returned 403 while the same URLs appear live and indexed in search results.

why_it_matters: The single most important buyer in this cell is not collectible with plain HTTP fetching. Collection must use a browser-based agent with realistic headers; and the source must NOT be recorded as dead.

description: No National Audit Office (ZKA/NAO) audit report specifically of BQK — and specifically of BQK procurement — was identified. BQK's financial statements appear to be audited by an external private auditor rather than covered in the NAO's budget-organisation audit programme.

result.result_summary: Two sq-language searches surfaced NAO's general annual audit report and BQK's own financial statements, but no NAO report on BQK.

why_it_matters: If BQK falls outside the NAO's audit universe, the 'audit report reveals the contract' mechanism in this cell's rationale does not apply to BQK itself — only to other regulators and ministries buying financial/IT services.

description: Both major civil-society mirrors show stale last-update dates: oshp.dplus.org last updated 16 Jan 2024, prokurimihapur.org last updated 27 Apr 2023.

result.result_summary: Both sites self-report update dates well over a year old as of Aug 2026.

why_it_matters: These are the best-structured views of the appeal and contract record. If they are no longer maintained, structured access must be rebuilt directly against oshp.rks-gov.net and e-prokurimi.rks-gov.net, which are far harder to parse.

description: KRPP announced the launch of a new website; legacy ASP.NET URLs of the form krpp.rks-gov.net/Default.aspx?LID=1&PID=Legislation may redirect or break.

result.result_summary: Search returned both legacy Default.aspx URLs and a new-look krpp.rks-gov.net root, plus a KRPP notice about 'funksionalizimin e webfaqes së re'.

why_it_matters: Any collector pinned to legacy KRPP URL patterns will silently break; a 404 here means moved, not dead.

description: Serbian-language (sr) coverage of this cell is materially thinner than Albanian. The only sr-language primary artefacts found were translated legal instruments (BQK procurement rules, KRPP instruction 002/2024, Law 2003/17) on the sq-primary domains — no sr-language notice board, sr-language OSHP decision search, or sr-language audit report was found.

result.result_summary: One dedicated sr query returned mostly translated legislation plus irrelevant regional central banks.

why_it_matters: Serbian-language collection for XK procurement should be scoped to the /srb/ or ?lang=sr document trees of the same official domains rather than treated as a separate source population; expecting a parallel sr ecosystem would waste crawl budget.

description: Targeted sq/mixed query for recent news on ATM and POS terminal supply contracts in Kosovo ('POS terminale' OR 'bankomatë' Kosovë kompani furnizim lajm 2025) returned only bank product/marketing pages and regional Serbian bank POS pages — no news articles naming a supplier or a contract.

result.result_summary: Zero media hits; results dominated by raiffeisen-kosovo.com, nlb-kos.com, teb-kos.com product pages and Serbian banks' POS pages.

why_it_matters: Confirms the cell premise inversely: supplier-side terminal contracts in Kosovo are largely invisible to general web search and will need site-scoped searching within each sq outlet plus bank corporate-news pages, not open-web queries.

description: The seed query 'nënshkruhet kontrata bankë Kosovë sistem pagesash' returned regulatory PDFs from BQK rather than any media report of a contract signing.

result.result_summary: All top results were BQK regulations on interbank payments and electronic payment instruments; no news item.

why_it_matters: The phrase 'sistem pagesash' is regulator-owned vocabulary and pulls legal texts. Media-facing queries need contract-ceremony vocabulary instead (nënshkruhet marrëveshja, memorandum bashkëpunimi, partneritet, lansohet) plus an outlet-scoped site: filter.

description: Preportr (COHU investigative journalism centre) did not appear in any result set this run despite being queried by name alongside Kallxo.

result.result_summary: Recorded as a candidate at reduced confidence with no example URLs; its domain is asserted from prior knowledge, not from an observed link.

why_it_matters: A named, on-topic procurement watchdog is missing from the evidence base; if the domain has moved, the highest-value long-form procurement source for Kosovo would be silently absent from the collection plan.

description: No RSS/Atom feed endpoints were confirmed for any of the sq outlets in this cell; no feed URL was observed in search results and no page was fetched to check for feed autodiscovery.

result.result_summary: Collection methods above therefore assume HTML listing-page polling.

why_it_matters: Feed availability materially changes collection cost and latency for a weak-signal channel that depends on being early. This needs a per-domain probe pass before the collector is built.

description: No specific Serbian-language tender or award notice for BANKING or PAYMENT services by a Serb-majority Kosovo municipality (Severna Mitrovica, Zvecan, Zubin Potok, Leposavic, Gracanica, Strpce, Klokot, Ranilug, Partes, Novo Brdo) was surfaced by general web search, despite multiple sr-language query formulations.

result.result_summary: Search engines surfaced the portals and the notice-form templates but not individual banking/payment award records; such notices appear to live inside portal search interfaces and PDF attachments that general indexes do not reach.

why_it_matters: Confirms that this cell cannot be covered by web search alone - collection must go through portal-internal search (e-prokurimi, prokurimihapur) rather than crawling the open web.

description: Several candidate URLs were identified only from search-result metadata and were not fetched in this pass (kosovo-online.com canonical domain, ekosova.rks-gov.net, Gracanica Online's own domain, EPS Elektrokosmet's dedicated procurement page).

result.result_summary: URLs are provided with reduced confidence_score; no liveness claim is made.

why_it_matters: The deterministic verification pass must resolve these before they enter the monitoring list; a 403/timeout on any of them should be treated as bot-defence, not death.

description: No established Serbian-language term set was found in this pass for modern payment-acceptance concepts as used in Kosovo procurement (e.g. POS terminals, card acquiring, instant payments). Serbian sources use Serbia-standard terms (POS terminali, prihvatanje kartica, instant placanja) whose actual usage in Kosovo Serbian-language tender text is unconfirmed.

result.result_summary: Glossary built confidently for procurement mechanics (ugovorni organ, obavestenje o dodeli ugovora, ekonomski operater, tenderska dokumentacija) but not for payment-technology nouns.

why_it_matters: Keyword filters built on Serbia-standard payments vocabulary may miss or over-match Kosovo Serbian-language notices, which are often translations from Albanian and use calqued wording.

description: It was not established whether the Serb-majority municipalities that operate parallel Serbia-recognised administrations publish procurement anywhere other than the Kosovo portal and their rks-gov.net sites - i.e. whether a parallel municipal procurement publication channel exists at all.

result.result_summary: Only Serbia-side central bodies (Kancelarija za KiM, EPS) were confirmed as parallel-structure buyers publishing on Serbian national channels; no parallel municipal-level publication venue was found.

why_it_matters: If parallel municipal spending is published nowhere, that spending is structurally invisible and must be inferred indirectly (media, Serbian budget line items, audit reports) rather than collected.

description: Direct fetch of the Kosovo Banking Association site (https://www.bankassoc-kos.com/Al/rreth-nesh/) returned HTTP 403 Forbidden.

result.result_summary: Treated as bot-defended-but-live hypothesis, not dead. Member names were partially recovered indirectly via a member bank's page (bkt-ks.com) and the association's Facebook page.

why_it_matters: The KBA member list is a primary pointer for the cell; a headless-browser collection path must be provisioned rather than assuming the source is unavailable.

description: Oda Ekonomike e Kosovës (OEK) does not expose a complete, browsable member directory in search-visible pages; only statute, departments and news were reachable.

result.result_summary: No 'lista e anëtarëve' page located for OEK despite Albanian-language querying.

why_it_matters: The statutory chamber would be the broadest supplier enumeration; without a directory, actor discovery must lean on STIKK, AmCham and OEGJK plus ARBK activity-code queries.

description: Albanian-language searching for a debarred/excluded economic operators register ('lista e operatorëve ekonomikë të përjashtuar') returned Republic of Albania results (app.gov.al) rather than Kosovo.

result.result_summary: No Kosovo (KRPP) debarment/economic-operator register URL confirmed in this pass.

why_it_matters: Shared Albanian terminology causes systematic Albania/Kosovo confusion; all sq queries for this run must be pinned with 'Kosovë', 'KRPP', 'rks-gov.net' to avoid contaminating the source list.

description: The 'Lista e Autoriteteve Kontraktuese' is referenced as a section of the e-Prokurimi portal but no stable deep URL to the list itself was observed.

result.result_summary: Only the portal root (e-prokurimi.rks-gov.net/Home/) and the annual-report PDFs were observed; the list URL is unconfirmed.

why_it_matters: Collection design must include a navigation step or a browser session against the portal rather than a fixed deep link.

description: Serbian-language (sr) searching surfaced only one Kosovo-specific chamber (Privredna komora Kosova i Metohije) and otherwise returned Serbia-proper institutions (APR, PKS regional chambers).

result.result_summary: No sr-language enumeration of Kosovo-licensed banks, payment firms or IT suppliers was found.

why_it_matters: Serb-majority-municipality actors and any sr-language procurement notices risk being under-covered; sr coverage of this cell is currently weak and should not be presented as complete.

description: Searched specifically for a Kosovo beneficial-ownership register ('regjistri i pronarëve përfitues'); no dedicated public BO register URL was identified.

result.result_summary: Ownership data appears reachable only via ARBK company records and third-party mirrors (ARBK Open, OpenCorporates, OCCRP Aleph).

why_it_matters: Ownership tracing behind tender awards will depend on registry extracts and aggregators, with the reliability caveats those carry.

description: No dedicated Kosovo-hosted fintech/payments conference with a published agenda and sponsor list was found for Pristina in 2026; the only clearly Kosovo-relevant payments event surfaced is the regional Balkan Payment Forum (organiser based outside Kosovo) plus BQK-hosted regulator conferences.

result.result_summary: Searches in sq and en returned generic global fintech-event calendars (Money20/20, eventbrowse, tapix, vendelux) rather than a Kosovo-specific payments expo.

why_it_matters: The cell's event-signal channel for Kosovo depends mainly on regulator-hosted conferences and regional events; there is no local trade expo whose exhibitor list can be harvested annually.

description: No specific LinkedIn or press announcement of a Kosovo bank or PSP naming a core-banking/payments implementation partner was located through open web search in this pass.

result.result_summary: Query returned generic vendor marketing (Skaleet, PSP Lab, sdk.finance) and one relevant institutional item (IFC/SECO partnership with BQK on digital financial services).

why_it_matters: Vendor-announcement signals for Kosovo appear to live behind LinkedIn's login wall rather than on the open web, so this channel likely needs licensed access or manual analyst review.

description: Serbian-language hiring/event signals specific to Kosovo banks are very thin: sr searches surfaced only generic Serbian job boards filtered to Kosovska Mitrovica, with no bank-specific 'konkurs' for a Kosovo-licensed bank found.

result.result_summary: sr query 'konkurs za posao banka Kosovo Mitrovica' returned board homepages, not bank adverts.

why_it_matters: sr is a mandated language for this run; the coverage exists only as a thin, low-yield channel and should not be assumed equivalent to the sq channel.

description: None of the URLs in this slice were fetched for liveness during this pass; all are recorded from search-result metadata and search-snippet content.

result.result_summary: Discovery-only pass; no fetch verdicts issued.

why_it_matters: Downstream deterministic verification must confirm reachability; absence of a fetch here is not evidence a source is dead.

description: Attempted to query the Internet Archive Wayback CDX API for the historical capture inventory of e-prokurimi.rks-gov.net, which is the canonical way to recover tender pages deleted from the live portal.

result.result_summary: The fetch tool returned 'Claude Code is unable to fetch from web.archive.org' — an environment-level restriction, not evidence that the Wayback Machine lacks Kosovo procurement captures. No conclusion can be drawn about actual archive coverage from this session.

why_it_matters: Web archives are named explicitly in this coverage cell and are the primary recovery route for removed tender pages. This capability gap must be closed by another means before the archival layer can be considered covered.

description: Searched in Albanian for a central, queryable register of expired or archived contract notices on e-prokurimi itself (arkivi i njoftimeve të skaduara).

result.result_summary: No dedicated public 'expired notices archive' interface was found on e-prokurimi.rks-gov.net. Historical notices appear to be reachable only through the OCDS API by date range, or via copies held on municipal and institutional websites. The portal's own front end appears to surface current activity.

why_it_matters: Confirms the premise of this cell: the archival layer must be reconstructed from the API plus third-party mirrors rather than read off a native archive view. It also means the OCDS date-range sweep is not optional — it is the only systematic route.

description: Searched in Albanian for a published register or archive of framework agreements specifically covering banking and payments equipment (ATMs, POS terminals, card personalisation, cash handling) for Kosovo public buyers.

result.result_summary: No sector-specific framework-agreement register was found. AQP's centralized contract listing is the correct register but the examples visible in search results were generic supply categories (paper, office materials, food, vehicles, fuel). Banking/payments framework contracts, if they exist, are not separately indexed and must be extracted by CPV/subject filtering over the full corpus.

why_it_matters: Sets realistic expectations for the collection design: sector targeting has to happen at the parse stage over a full-corpus sweep, not by finding a ready-made vertical register.

description: Searched for a procurement notice or contract archive on the Central Bank of Kosovo (BQK) website, which as a payments-sector buyer and regulator would be a priority contracting authority.

result.result_summary: Only BQK annual institutional/financial reports surfaced (bqk-kos.org, including a wp-content/uploads PDF tree). No procurement-specific notice archive or contract register was located for BQK in this pass. This is unverified absence, not confirmed absence — the site was not crawled directly.

why_it_matters: BQK is among the most relevant single buyers for this run's sector focus. If it has no published procurement archive, its awards must be recovered from the central KRPP OCDS feed by partyName, and the BQK annual report becomes the fallback source for capital-expenditure signals.

description: Attempted to read the KRPP institutional homepage (krpp.rks-gov.net) to enumerate its navigation, annual-report index and archive sections.

result.result_summary: The fetch returned only the page title 'KOMISIONI RREGULLATIV I PROKURIMIT PUBLIK' with no navigation or links, consistent with a JavaScript-rendered single-page front end. This is a rendering limitation and a hypothesis of client-side rendering, not evidence the site is dead — the sibling e-prokurimi document paths resolve normally.

why_it_matters: The report and archive index on krpp.rks-gov.net may only be reachable via a headless browser or an underlying JSON endpoint. Until then, annual reports must be addressed by direct document-path enumeration on e-prokurimi.rks-gov.net rather than by following site navigation.

description: Fetched the PPRC 2022 English annual report PDF to confirm liveness and inspect its statistical tables.

result.result_summary: A 2.2 MB application/pdf payload was returned, so the /eng/ document path is populated, but the fetch tool could not extract text from the binary and the statistical table inventory could not be confirmed in this pass. Treat the URL as promising-but-unparsed; liveness verification remains the job of the separate deterministic pass.

why_it_matters: The annual-report series is the backbone of the statistical layer for this cell. Collection tooling must include a real PDF text/table extractor, since a plain fetch-to-markdown step will silently fail on this entire source family.

description: Serbian-language (sr) searching for a Kosovo procurement archive returned markedly thinner results than Albanian, and several hits were for the separate Serbian and Montenegrin national procurement systems rather than Kosovo.

result.result_summary: Serbian terms did work — Regulatorna komisija za javne nabavke (RKJN), javne nabavke, ugovori, godišnji izveštaj, arhiva — and yielded the D+ institutional analysis, the ZKA Serbian publications path (/sr/), and the legacy Assembly legislative archive in Serbian. But no Serbian-language archive of Kosovo tender notices or a Serbian edition of the PPRC annual report series was located.

why_it_matters: Serbian-language procurement records matter for northern municipalities and Serb-majority contracting authorities. The apparent absence may reflect genuine non-publication in Serbian, or a search-reach limitation; either way the sr layer of this cell is not yet demonstrably covered.

description: Looked for a bulk export, API, or open-data download from the civil-society prokurimihapur.org portal, which holds pre-2016 contract data unavailable elsewhere.

result.result_summary: The about page documents a web UI (Contracts, Buyers, Suppliers, Network, Report) and states data are freely accessible in readable format, but names no API and no bulk download. Programmatic access would require HTML scraping or a direct request to Lëvizja FOL.

why_it_matters: The 2010–2016 window is only practically covered by this portal, so the absence of bulk export is the main friction point for extending the historical baseline behind the OCDS start date.

description: Direct fetch of https://kk.rks-gov.net/prishtine/prokurimi/njoftim-per-kontrate/ failed with getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND kk.rks-gov.net from this environment.

result.result_summary: DNS did not resolve. This is a HYPOTHESIS of an egress/geo/DNS restriction on this host, NOT evidence the site is dead — the domain appears as a live indexed result under at least two different municipality slugs (prishtine, skenderaj). Must be re-attempted by the deterministic verification pass, ideally from a European egress.

why_it_matters: kk.rks-gov.net is the backbone of this entire cell (~38 municipalities). If it stays unreachable from the collection host, municipal-level banking tenders — the single densest and lowest-visibility segment — are lost.

description: Serbian-language search for Kosovo municipal banking-services tenders (opština / javne nabavke / bankarske usluge / platni promet / obaveštenje o ugovoru) returned almost entirely Serbia, Montenegro and Bosnia sources, not Kosovo authorities.

result.result_summary: The only Kosovo-specific sr-language hit was the official Serbian translation of the public procurement instruction on e-prokurimi.rks-gov.net. No Serbian-language procurement page of a Kosovo municipality (e.g. the four northern municipalities) was located in this pass.

why_it_matters: Kosovo law provides for Serbian as an official language and Serb-majority municipalities are genuine contracting authorities with their own banking arrangements. Failing to reach them leaves a language-and-territory hole, and sr-language queries also risk polluting the corpus with Serbia-proper tenders that must be filtered out.

description: No authority-hosted notice explicitly for bank current-account / salary-payment / e-payment-gateway services was retrieved during this pass.

result.result_summary: Local-language terms were used ('shërbime bankare', 'llogari rrjedhëse', 'pagesa elektronike', 'arkëtim', 'bankarske usluge', 'platni promet') but search surfaced the procurement PAGES rather than any matching individual notice. The observed authority-hosted notices were for other categories (insurance, lab equipment, uniforms, books, oils).

why_it_matters: Confirms the cell's core thesis needs document-level crawling, not search-engine discovery: these notices exist as PDFs inside listing pages that search engines index poorly. Budget for full-text PDF harvesting rather than query-based discovery.

description: No own-site procurement page located for several important buyers: KEK (kek-energy.com), Trepça Sh.A., regional water utilities (Ujësjellësi Rajonal), and SHSKUK / individual hospitals.

result.result_summary: These authorities were confirmed to exist and to procure, but only via the central portal, media reporting, or aggregators. Their own procurement URLs were not identified in this pass.

why_it_matters: POEs and hospitals are large-payroll, high-cash-handling buyers. If they publish only centrally, the cell's added value for them is zero and coverage should be delegated to the central-portal cell instead of duplicated here.

description: UN Development Business (devbusiness.un.org), historically the mandated publication channel for World Bank and MCC General Procurement Notices, is reported to have phased down operations and ceased website activity on 31 March 2025.

result.result_summary: Search results state UNDB ceased activity; legacy notice URLs such as https://devbusiness.un.org/notices/cdb-p836201 may persist as archive only. Not independently fetch-verified in this pass — treat as unverified hypothesis, not a confirmed death.

why_it_matters: Any collection design that anchors on UNDB for donor GPNs will silently return nothing post-2025; the pipeline must be rebuilt on projects.worldbank.org, ECEPP, dgMarket and implementing-entity sites, and historical UNDB pages should be pulled from web archives while they last.

description: No dedicated procurement or tender page was found for the Deposit Insurance Fund of Kosovo (Fondi i Sigurimit të Depozitave në Kosovë) or the Kosovo Credit Guarantee Fund (Fondi Kosovar për Garanci Kreditore), despite both being named implementing agencies of the World Bank Financial Sector Development Project.

result.result_summary: Albanian-language search on 'prokurim', 'tender', 'ftesë për ofertë' plus both institution names returned institutional/Facebook/LinkedIn pages and enabling legislation, but no procurement board on fondikgk.org or an FSDK site.

why_it_matters: Two of the three FSDP implementing agencies may publish their notices only inside World Bank channels or on social media, meaning a site-level watcher would miss them. Collection should lean on the WB notice portal and on the institutions' Facebook/LinkedIn feeds as a fallback.

description: Serbian-language searching for donor-funded financial-sector tenders in Kosovo returned almost no Kosovo-specific procurement surface.

result.result_summary: Query 'Kosovo tender javni poziv nabavka finansijski sektor projekat finansiran od EU' returned mostly Serbia-focused portals (euzatebe.rs, evropa.gov.rs, tenderteam.rs) plus one generic aggregator page for Kosovo and EEAS Serbian-language press releases.

why_it_matters: Donor procurement notices for Kosovo appear to be published in Albanian and English, with Serbian used mainly for political/communications output rather than tender documents. Serbian-language monitoring should target EEAS _sr press releases and Serbian-language Kosovo media rather than tender boards, and Serbian coverage should not be treated as a parity requirement for this cell.

description: Commercial tender aggregators (tendersinfo.com, tendersontime.com, globaltenders.com, biddetail.com, javne-nabavke.com, developmentaid.org) dominate search results for almost every donor+Kosovo query.

result.result_summary: These sites rank highly, present recycled or SEO-generated 'Kosovo Tenders 2026' pages, and gate actual notice content behind subscriptions; several appear to restate notices without a verifiable primary link.

why_it_matters: They are a credibility and cost trap: high recall, low verifiability, restrictive ToS. They should be excluded from automated collection and used at most for lead generation with mandatory resolution back to the issuing donor's own notice.

description: EBRD, EIB and IFC financial-intermediary operations in Kosovo (credit lines to commercial banks, guarantees, equity, advisory) generate no public procurement notice at all.

result.result_summary: The Kosovo EBRD financial-sector activity found in this pass (e.g. up to EUR 5m to a Kosovo bank under Go Digital in the Western Balkans with EU-funded incentives) surfaced only as a press release, not as any tender.

why_it_matters: A procurement-notice-only collection strategy will systematically under-count private-sector donor money flowing into Kosovo bank digitalisation. Project Summary Documents, press releases and disclosure registers must be collected alongside tender feeds to see this spend.

description: Albanian-language searching for EU Office in Kosovo financial-sector tender calls ('Zyra e BE-së në Kosovë thirrje për tender sektori financiar') returned no dedicated sq-language tender listing page.

result.result_summary: Results surfaced the delegation's institutional sq pages (kush-jemi-ne_sq, bashkimi-evropian-dhe-kosova_sq) and a job board, not tender notices. EU-channel tender notices for Kosovo appear to be published predominantly in English, with only institutional/communication content localised into sq.

why_it_matters: Confirms the cell's premise: for EU-level procurement the working language is English, so sq/sr querying is useful mainly for actor names and glossary, not for finding the notices themselves. Collection design should not depend on sq-language tender feeds.

description: Serbian-language search for EU Office in Kosovo procurement ('Kancelarija Evropske unije na Kosovu javne nabavke tenderi poziv') found no official sr-language EU tender feed for Kosovo.

result.result_summary: Only third-party sr aggregators (javne-nabavke.com, nabavke.com) republishing EEAS notices, plus the delegation's sr 'ko smo mi' page naming the Finance and Contracts Section (Odsek za finansije i ugovore, delegation-kosovo-fincon@eeas.europa.eu).

why_it_matters: sr-language coverage of this cell must be obtained via commercial aggregators or by translating English notices; there is no primary sr channel to monitor.

description: No Kosovo central-bank / banking-supervision Twinning fiche was located in this pass.

result.result_summary: Search surfaced Kosovo twinning fiches in other sectors (personal data protection, public finance, media) and a regional 'Strengthening Central Bank Capacities in the Western Balkans' programme naming CBK/BQK as beneficiary, but no Kosovo-specific banking-supervision twinning fiche document.

why_it_matters: Either such a fiche does not exist (Kosovo central-bank support may run through regional ESCB programmes and IMF/WB rather than twinning) or it is buried in non-indexed PDFs. Needs a dedicated deeper pass before concluding.

description: FTS coverage of IPA Kosovo contracts is structurally incomplete.

result.result_summary: EC guidance encountered in results states that for IPA one should consult national IPA coordinators rather than the Financial Transparency System, because a share of IPA is not under direct management.

why_it_matters: Any vendor-level analysis built on FTS alone will systematically under-count Kosovo IPA contracts; must be complemented with TED award notices and DG ENEST/IATI beneficiary data.

description: No source in this slice was fetched or liveness-tested; all URLs are search-derived.

result.result_summary: This pass used web search only. Some URLs (notably the wbif.eu root, the EIB TA calls index, the DG ENEST twinning landing page and the EEAS Kosovo delegation root) are constructed from known site structure rather than observed in a result snippet, and are flagged with lower confidence.

why_it_matters: The deterministic verification pass must resolve these; a 403/404 on any of them should be treated as a hypothesis to re-check, not proof the source is dead.

description: ProCredit Bank Kosova (procreditbank-kos.com) has no discoverable tender, RFP or supplier-registration page. Site-scoped searches in Albanian ('ftesë për ofertë', 'shpallje', 'furnizim', 'tender') returned only product, pricing and news pages, while sibling ProCredit entities in Serbia, Georgia, Ukraine and Albania all expose /tenders paths.

result.result_summary: Kosovo entity appears to run procurement privately or via the holding, publishing nothing locally; a direct fetch of its business-ethics page also returned HTTP 500 (unverified, not dead).

why_it_matters: ProCredit is a systemic Kosovo bank; if its RFPs are invisible, its IT/card/self-service buying can only be inferred from vendor announcements, group signals or interviews, leaving a real blind spot in A2 coverage.

description: Ziraat Bank Kosova SHA exposes no tender, procurement or supplier page; only a general 'Lajmërime/announcements' feed. Turkish-parent procurement terminology ('ihale') was not tested against the Kosovo domain because the site publishes only sq/en.

result.result_summary: No procurement surface located for Ziraat Kosovo.

why_it_matters: A locally incorporated Turkish-parent bank undergoing legal transformation is likely to be buying systems now, invisibly.

description: No open group-level supplier-registration or e-sourcing portal was found for RBI (rbinternational.com resolves to a platform login), for NLB Group (no 'javna naročila'/'dobavitelji' portal on nlb.si or nlbgroup.com), or for ProCredit Holding. Searched in de/sl/sr/en.

result.result_summary: Foreign parents do not run public vendor portals reachable without authentication; RBI's supplier code even prohibits suppliers disclosing anything about pending group procurements.

why_it_matters: The cell rationale assumed group procurement portals would be a route into Kosovo subsidiary buying; they are not. Collection must lean on local bank pages, vendor-side announcements and human sourcing.

description: Serbian-language queries ('javne nabavke', 'dobavljači', 'tender ponuda') for Kosovo commercial banks returned Serbia-based portals (nbs.rs, nabavke.com, javne-nabavke.com, tenderbiro.rs) and no Kosovo bank content; the sole Kosovo hit was the Albanian NLB notice page.

result.result_summary: Kosovo commercial banks appear not to publish procurement notices in Serbian, even though it is an official language.

why_it_matters: Serbian-language monitoring for this cell should be reweighted toward North Kosovo / Serbia-facing media and vendor sources rather than bank tender pages; it is not a productive channel for bank RFPs.

description: None of the Kosovo bank tender pages examined (NLB, TEB, BKT, Banka Ekonomike, BPB, Raiffeisen) published award results, winning bidder names or contract values — only invitations, specifications and deadline extensions.

result.result_summary: Award-notice coverage for private bank procurement in Kosovo is effectively zero.

why_it_matters: The 'award notices' topic in this run cannot be satisfied from private-buyer sources; outcomes must be reconstructed from vendor press releases, reference lists, LinkedIn and observed deployments.

description: bkt-ks.com returned a TLS chain error ('unable to verify the first certificate') on direct fetch, while its tender URLs are fully present in the search index.

result.result_summary: Treated as bot/TLS-configuration friction, not as a dead source.

why_it_matters: A naive collector would wrongly mark one of the richest tender feeds in the cell as unreachable.

description: No public tender portal, notice board or RFP feed operated by any Kosovo licensed payment institution, e-money institution or remittance firm was found. Searched in sq ('tender', 'njoftim për kontratë', 'furnizim me terminale POS') and en against company sites (UFP, Moneta, OneFor, Swinto, IBAS, Paysera Kosova).

result.result_summary: Private payment-sector procurement in Kosovo appears to be entirely unpublished; only corporate news, partner press and job ads reveal it.

why_it_matters: Coverage of this cell cannot rely on tender feeds — it must be built from the licence register plus company/partner/vendor announcement monitoring, which changes the collection design and expected latency.

description: No independent third-party card switch, processor or ATM/POS network operator serving Kosovo was identified. Searches in en and sq repeatedly returned only BQK (operator of the sole payment system, the Interbank Payment System) and individual banks' own acquiring.

result.result_summary: Switching/processing appears to be bank-internal or outsourced abroad rather than run by a domestic non-bank processor.

why_it_matters: If confirmed, the 'processor' segment of this cell is empty domestically and terminal/switching demand sits with banks and with foreign processors — a materially different buyer map than assumed in the cell definition.

description: Two bqk-kos.org URLs (the licensed-institutions list PDF and the non-bank financial institutions section page) returned HTTP 403 on fetch, although both are indexed and linked from search results.

result.result_summary: Hypothesis: bot defence / user-agent filtering on the BQK web server, not removal.

why_it_matters: The single most important register in this cell needs a browser-grade fetcher; a naive crawler would wrongly record it as dead.

description: Serbian-language (sr) searching produced no Kosovo-specific non-bank payments procurement sources. Cyrillic queries on Kosovo payment processing tenders returned only Serbia-domestic material (NBS tariffs, Serbian banks, KZK case files).

result.result_summary: sr coverage of this cell is effectively empty at the search-engine level; north-Kosovo payment arrangements were not surfaced by these queries.

why_it_matters: The Serbian-language segment of Kosovo's payments landscape (Serbian-system institutions and cash/remittance channels in the north) may be systematically invisible to this method and needs a targeted approach.

description: Several fintechs surfaced (IBAS, Swinto, UPay) describe themselves as licensed e-money or payment platforms serving Kosovo, but their licensing jurisdiction was not confirmed against the BQK register within this run.

result.result_summary: Names captured as candidates with reduced credibility scores pending register cross-check.

why_it_matters: Treating an EU-licensed firm as a BQK licensee would distort the buyer universe for this cell.

description: No Kosovo-specific contract-win press release was found on Asseco SEE's or Payten's newsrooms via search, despite both having a Kosovo presence (ASSECO SEE SH.P.K.) and heavy regional announcement activity.

result.result_summary: Searches returned only Serbia/Croatia/North Macedonia bank announcements. Payten news listing fetched directly showed five recent items, none Kosovo-related.

why_it_matters: Suggests Kosovo wins by the dominant regional vendor group are either not announced or announced only in local/LinkedIn channels — collection must include vendor LinkedIn feeds and local-language press, not only corporate newsrooms.

description: Albanian-language and Serbian-language searches for vendor-announced Kosovo bank contracts returned no supply-side announcements at all.

result.result_summary: sq query ('Kosovë bankë kontratë sistem bankar zbatim kompani IT zgjidhje softuerike') and sr query ('banka Kosovo bankarski softver ugovor implementacija integrator') both returned generic banking-sector material (BQK documents, Wikipedia, academic theses), not vendor press releases.

why_it_matters: Local-language general web search is a weak channel for this cell; the productive local-language route is likely vendor/bank LinkedIn posts and local business media, which general search engines index poorly.

description: printec.eu is NOT the banking-technology Printec.

result.result_summary: Fetch of https://www.printec.eu/ returned a German-language decorative-lighting company (references_fashion, products_decorative_lights). The banking integrator is printecgroup.com, which returned HTTP 403 to a plain fetch.

why_it_matters: Prevents a false-positive source and a wasted monitoring pipeline; also flags that printecgroup.com needs browser-like fetching.

description: No evidence found of a named Kosovo bank running Temenos, Oracle FLEXCUBE, BPC SmartVista or OpenWay Way4.

result.result_summary: Vendor-name + Kosovo searches surfaced only generic product-comparison pages and technographics teasers; no vendor case study or press release naming a Kosovo institution.

why_it_matters: The core-banking/switch layer for Kosovo banks remains unattributed; this is the single biggest unknown in the supply-side picture and should drive targeted collection (RFP documents, bank annual reports, job ads naming systems).

description: printecgroup.com returned HTTP 403 on WebFetch.

result.result_summary: Single failed fetch; almost certainly bot defence rather than a dead site (the company is active and has a Kosovo entity registered per D&B).

why_it_matters: Must not be recorded as dead; requires a headless-browser or header-spoofing collector.

description: No aggregator or open-contracting dataset was found that is scoped specifically to banking, payments, cards, POS or ATM procurement in Kosovo.

result.result_summary: Every aggregator located is generalist (all-sector) and must be filtered by CPV code or keyword. Searching explicitly for banking/ATM/card tender aggregation for Kosovo returned only generic country pages and IFI portals.

why_it_matters: Collection design must own the sector filtering layer (CPV + Albanian/Serbian keyword lists); no vendor supplies a ready-made banking-sector Kosovo feed.

description: Kosovo's OCDS publication has documented structural gaps and a stale quality review.

result.result_summary: The OCP registry entry reports ~211k parties and ~75.7k tenders but zero counts for awards, contracts and planning; the awards array is misspelled 'award'; procuringEntity sits in a non-standard location; Lots extension fields have typos; last quality review November 2021.

why_it_matters: Award-notice coverage — the part that reveals who actually won banking/IT contracts — cannot be assumed present in the OCDS feed alone; a second source (Integrity Watch, Prokurimi i Hapur, or the portal itself) is required for awards.

description: Prokurimi i Hapur may not be refreshing.

result.result_summary: The site states data is currently being updated through the API system and asks users to report errors; the most recent update date observed on the page was 27 April 2023.

why_it_matters: If the portal is frozen, it remains valuable as a historical archive but cannot serve as a live monitoring feed. Needs a liveness check before it is wired into a pipeline.

description: Serbian-language aggregator coverage of Kosovo is thin and politically framed.

result.result_summary: Serbian-language searching surfaced only one aggregator with a real Kosovo section (javne-nabavke.com) plus a regional player (eKapija) whose stated coverage is BiH/Serbia/Montenegro. The Kosovo page's top-buyer list leads with a Serbia-administered provisional municipal body, indicating partial rather than national coverage.

why_it_matters: Serbian-language collection cannot be relied on for full Kosovo coverage; sq and en remain the primary languages, with sr used mainly for Serb-majority municipality and cross-border angles.

description: dgMarket was referenced as a procurement aggregator but no Kosovo-specific dgMarket endpoint was located.

result.result_summary: Search results mentioned dgMarket only second-hand via a donor page; no dgMarket Kosovo country URL was reached in this pass.

why_it_matters: dgMarket historically aggregated World Bank/donor notices; if still active it would fill the IFI channel. Should be re-checked directly rather than recorded as absent.

description: Several commercial aggregators' Kosovo coverage depth could not be measured without a paid subscription.

result.result_summary: TendersInfo, GlobalTenders, TenderImpulse, TendersGo and TendersOnTime all advertise Kosovo coverage, but the actual notice count, latency and whether they carry award notices is behind a paywall/registration wall.

why_it_matters: Their marketing claims must not be recorded as verified coverage; a trial-based bake-off against the OCDS feed is needed before any is paid for.

description: No Kosovo watchdog or investigative outlet was found publishing a dedicated investigation into procurement of BANKING or PAYMENT services specifically (e.g. state treasury banking services, card acquiring, POS/ATM supply, payment-system IT contracts).

result.result_summary: Searches in sq, sr and en combining bank/payment terms with tender/procurement terms returned generic banking-sector coverage (bank complaints, bank stability) or generic procurement coverage, but no bank-services award investigation.

why_it_matters: The watchdog ecosystem is strong on infrastructure, energy and vehicle contracts; banking/payments procurement appears to be an unwatched niche, so this cell will need keyword-level monitoring of raw award data rather than relying on ready-made investigations.

description: Transparency International has no standalone national chapter website for Kosovo; TI-related procurement monitoring surfaces through the Kosovo Democratic Institute (KDI) as national contact.

result.result_summary: Searches for a 'Transparency International Kosovo' site returned KDI publications and TI regional/global index references instead.

why_it_matters: Collection should target kdi-kosova.org rather than looking for a TI-XK domain that likely does not exist.

description: Democracy Plus reports the official OSHP (Procurement Review Body) website has had problems since December 2025, with documents older than six months inaccessible.

result.result_summary: Reported by D+ and echoed in Kosovo media (Epoka e Re, Aug 2026) as part of a wider public-institution web transparency crisis.

why_it_matters: Official appeal-decision provenance is unreliable; the CSO mirror at oshp.dplus.org becomes the de-facto archive of record and should be collected proactively before it too goes stale.

description: Two Serbian-language watchdog domains (newsocialinitiative.org, ngoaktiv.org) were inferred from organisation names in third-party coverage rather than confirmed by a direct fetch.

result.result_summary: Their procurement work is documented via Alternativna and Radio Mitrovica Sever coverage; own sites not opened during this pass.

why_it_matters: These are the only Serbian-language procurement-monitoring producers found; a wrong domain would silently drop sr-language coverage of the north.

description: No Kosovo-specific document-leak or whistleblower publishing platform (SecureDrop-style) dedicated to procurement documents was identified beyond KALLXO's general corruption-reporting intake.

result.result_summary: KALLXO functions as the citizen reporting intake; no separate leaked-contract repository surfaced.

why_it_matters: Underlying contract PDFs will mostly have to come from e-Prokurimi/OPTP or from documents embedded in individual articles.
